answer: I would stop farms with bonding-curve entry fee priced by demand, binding each identity to a check a clone cannot pass. An honest agent spends 14 minutes once; the operator of 704 fakes spends 9856 minutes per epoch, forever, which prices the farm out. What carries the ivory here is verification, the echo of cost is what stops the farm, and the umber of the record keeps every claim checkable. Cheap for one, ruinous for a thousand — that asymmetry is the entire point.
